messages.subject: Sexpr conditional evaluation
parts:
I have used knitr in the past to create a homework assignment and, based on a logical object, a homework answer key.  A minimal example is below (as it is set right now the assignment but not the answer key would be created).  This procedure worked in the past (roughly 9 months ago, I don’t know with which version of knitr) but it does not now, sending the error that object b cannot be found on line 15 (the line with the \Sexpr).  It seems that the problem is that the \Sexpr{} is always evaluated and if it returns an error then the compilation ends.  Is there a way to conditionally stop the evaluation of \Sexpr or to have the compilation not stop on errors (if there is an error in a chunk then the compilation does not stop)?  Alternatively, can someone suggest another solution?  [I imagine an inelegant solution is to have eval=TRUE always and then conditionally use echo=FALSE and results=”hide”.]

 

Thanks in advance for any help.

 

\documentclass{article}

\newif\ifdothis

 

\begin{document}

<<echo=FALSE>>=

dothis <- FALSE  # change to TRUE to show answer key

@

%\dothistrue    % uncomment to show answer key

 

The question is what is b?

<<eval=dothis, echo=dothis>>=

b <- 7

@

 

\ifdothis

The answer is \Sexpr{b}.

\fi

 

\end{document}

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Sexpr conditional evaluation
parts:
Yes, I made a change in the development version of knitr a while ago:
if there is an error in \Sexpr{}, knitr will stop. In the past, the
evaluation was done in try() by default, so it will never stop. There
are two possible workarounds on my mind:

1. use try() explicitly in \Sexpr{}, e.g. \Sexpr{try(b)};

2. use a chunk hook instead of LaTeX programming, e.g.

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

<<echo=FALSE>>=
dothis <- FALSE # change to TRUE to show answer key

opts_knit$set(eval.after = 'answer')
knit_hooks$set(answer = function(before, options, envir) {
if (dothis && !before) do.call(sprintf, options$answer)
})
@
The question is what is b?

<<eval=dothis, echo=dothis, answer=list("The answer is %s.", b)>>=
b <- 7
@
\end{document}


Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: RE: [knitr] Sexpr conditional evaluation
parts:
Yihui et al.,

Thanks for the help. I did not use either of your workarounds. I have several \Sexpr{} in my real document so I did not want to put try() in each of those. Also, my "answers" are often more like a paragraph so the hook work-around did not seem reasonable either. The workaround that I ended up using was to evaluate everything all of the time and then use my dothis logical to toggle whether results="markup" or results="hide". Thus, the minimal example I sent before was modified as shown below. The result was really only one more line of code and replacing all of my eval= with results= values.

As always, thanks for your useful and prompt help.

-----

\documentclass{article}
\newif\ifdothis

\begin{document}
<<echo=FALSE>>=
dothis <- FALSE # change to TRUE to show answer key
doresults <- ifelse(dothis,"markup","hide")

@
%\dothistrue % uncomment to show answer key

The question is what is b?
<<echo=dothis, results=doresults>>=

b <- 7
@

\ifdothis
The answer is \Sexpr{b}.
\fi

\end{document}
